Hi David / team —

Thanks for the questions — answers below and next steps to keep things moving.

1) SOC 2: Attached is a redacted SOC 2 Type II report covering security & availability controls (secops sections redacted). We can provide a full report under NDA if required. Link for our compliance portal: https://drive.redwood.ai/soc2/redacted_2025

2) BAA & eligible deployments: Redwood will sign a Business Associate Agreement for customers who deploy in either Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC / on-prem) modes. Hosted/public API is not eligible for PHI/BAA due to shared tenancy and logging/profileing policies. 

3) PHI handling constraints: 
- PHI is acceptable on Dedicated and Private only.
- We do not index or use PHI to improve models; we can configure no-persist logging and strict KV cache controls for PHI flows.
- KMS: For Private we support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). For Dedicated we can integrate with cloud KMS and offer customer key options — we'll scope this with Dev.
- Retention and auditing: audit logs available for Dedicated/Private deployments; retention windows configurable based on contract.

4) Volume & eligibility: your pilot volume (~5k messages/month) is modest — eligibility is determined by deployment mode rather than strict throughput. If you need BAA coverage, we should plan for Dedicated or Private from the start. We can discuss a short Dedicated pilot if you want predictable throughput without full on-prem.

Next steps (proposed):
- Dev will connect with your infra/security team to answer questionnaire items and scope KMS/network. (Action: Dev / MedCare IT)
- Legal: please review the attached draft BAA (Redwood_Draft_BAA_MedCare_20260806.pdf) and propose redlines. (Action: MedCare Legal)
- I'll open a HubSpot deal record and add the SOC2 + BAA artifacts. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/67890
